speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते ।
ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् ॥
iast:
śreyo hi jñānamabhyāsājjñānāddhyānaṃ viśiṣyate |
dhyānātkarmaphalatyāgastyāgācchāntiranantaram ||
english: Knowledge is better than practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation; and from giving up comes peace at once.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च ।
निर्ममो निरहंकारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥
iast:
adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca |
nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī ||
english: One who bears no hatred towards any being, who is friendly and compassionate, free of possessiveness and ego, the same in pain and pleasure, and forgiving,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
संतुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः ।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
iast:
saṃtuṣṭaḥ satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ |
mayyarpitamanobuddhiryo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||
english: always content, disciplined, self-controlled and firm in resolve, with mind and understanding offered to me: that devotee of mine is dear to me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः ।
हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥
iast:
yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ |
harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
english: One from whom the world does not shrink, and who does not shrink from the world, who is free of elation, impatience, fear and agitation, is dear to me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः ।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
iast:
anapekṣaḥ śucirdakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ |
sarvārambhaparityāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||
english: One who expects nothing, who is pure, capable, impartial and free of anxiety, who has given up all self-centred undertakings: that devotee of mine is dear to me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥
iast:
yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
śubhāśubhaparityāgī bhaktimānyaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||
english: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, who has let go of both good and bad outcomes, and is full of devotion, is dear to me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः ।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥
iast:
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ |
śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ ||
english: One who is the same towards enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, the same in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, free of attachment,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येन केनचित् ।
अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
iast:
tulyanindāstutirmaunī santuṣṭo yena kenacit |
aniketaḥ sthiramatirbhaktimānme priyo naraḥ ||
english: to whom blame and praise are the same, who is restrained in speech, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady of mind and full of devotion: that person is dear to me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते ।
श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः ॥
iast:
ye tu dharmyāmṛtamidaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate |
śraddadhānā matparamā bhaktāste'tīva me priyāḥ ||
english: But those who, with faith and taking me as the highest, follow this immortal dharma as I have taught it, those devotees are exceedingly dear to me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते ।
एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥
iast:
idaṃ śarīraṃ kaunteya kṣetramityabhidhīyate |
etadyo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ ||
english: This body, son of Kunti, is called the field; the one who knows it is called the knower of the field by those who know these things.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत ।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम ॥
iast:
kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata |
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorjñānaṃ yattajjñānaṃ mataṃ mama ||
english: Know me, too, as the knower of the field in all fields, Arjuna. Knowledge of the field and of its knower is, in my view, true knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक्च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् ।
स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु ॥
iast:
tatkṣetraṃ yacca yādṛkca yadvikāri yataśca yat |
sa ca yo yatprabhāvaśca tatsamāsena me śṛṇu ||
english: Hear from me in brief what the field is, what it is like, what changes it undergoes and where it comes from, and who its knower is and what powers that knower has.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् ।
ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्चितैः ॥
iast:
ṛṣibhirbahudhā gītaṃ chandobhirvividhaiḥ pṛthak |
brahmasūtrapadaiścaiva hetumadbhirviniścitaiḥ ||
english: This has been sung by sages in many ways, separately in various Vedic hymns, and in the reasoned and conclusive verses of the Brahma Sutras.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
महाभूतान्यहंकारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च ।
इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः ॥
iast:
mahābhūtānyahaṃkāro buddhiravyaktameva ca |
indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca pañca cendriyagocarāḥ ||
english: The great elements, the sense of 'I', the intellect and the unmanifest; the ten senses and the mind; and the five objects of the senses;

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं संघातश्चेतना धृतिः ।
एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् ॥
iast:
icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃghātaścetanā dhṛtiḥ |
etatkṣetraṃ samāsena savikāramudāhṛtam ||
english: desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the body as a whole, awareness and steadiness: this, in brief, is the field together with its changes.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् ।
आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः ॥
iast:
amānitvamadambhitvamahiṃsā kṣāntirārjavam |
ācāryopāsanaṃ śaucaṃ sthairyamātmavinigrahaḥ ||
english: Humility, lack of pretence, non-violence, patience, honesty, service to one's teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहंकार एव च ।
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् ॥
iast:
indriyārtheṣu vairāgyamanahaṃkāra eva ca |
janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanam ||
english: dispassion towards the objects of the senses, absence of ego, and clearly seeing the trouble and pain of birth, death, old age and sickness;

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु ।
नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु ॥
iast:
asaktiranabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu |
nityaṃ ca samacittatvamiṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu ||
english: non-attachment, not clinging to son, wife, home and the like, and constant evenness of mind amid what is welcome and what is unwelcome;

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी ।
विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि ॥
iast:
mayi cānanyayogena bhaktiravyabhicāriṇī |
viviktadeśasevitvamaratirjanasaṃsadi ||
english: unswerving devotion to me through single-minded yoga, resorting to solitary places, and no taste for crowds;

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम् ।
एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा ॥
iast:
adhyātmajñānanityatvaṃ tattvajñānārthadarśanam |
etajjñānamiti proktamajñānaṃ yadato'nyathā ||
english: constancy in knowledge of the self, and insight into the purpose of true knowledge: this is called knowledge, and whatever is contrary to it is ignorance.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वामृतमश्नुते ।
अनादि मत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते ॥
iast:
jñeyaṃ yattatpravakṣyāmi yajjñātvāmṛtamaśnute |
anādi matparaṃ brahma na sattannāsaducyate ||
english: I will describe what is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality: the beginningless supreme Brahman, which is said to be neither being nor non-being.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् ।
सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥
iast:
sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tatsarvato'kṣiśiromukham |
sarvataḥ śrutimalloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati ||
english: It has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and faces everywhere, and ears everywhere in the world; it stands enveloping all.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् ।
असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च ॥
iast:
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam |
asaktaṃ sarvabhṛccaiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca ||
english: It seems to have the qualities of all the senses, yet is free of all the senses; unattached, yet sustaining all; free of the gunas, yet experiencing the gunas.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च ।
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् ॥
iast:
bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraṃ carameva ca |
sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat ||
english: It is outside and inside beings, unmoving and moving; it is too subtle to be known; it is far away, and also near.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् ।
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥
iast:
avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam |
bhūtabhartṛ ca tajjñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca ||
english: Undivided, it seems divided among beings; it is to be known as the sustainer of beings, the one who devours them and the one who brings them forth.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते ।
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम् ॥
iast:
jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate |
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam ||
english: It is the light of all lights, said to be beyond darkness; it is knowledge, what is to be known, and the goal of knowledge, dwelling in the heart of all.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः ।
मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते ॥
iast:
iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ |
madbhakta etadvijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate ||
english: So the field, knowledge and what is to be known have been described in brief. My devotee who understands this comes to my state of being.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि ।
विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान् ॥
iast:
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhyanādī ubhāvapi |
vikārāṃśca guṇāṃścaiva viddhi prakṛtisaṃbhavān ||
english: Know that both nature and the person are without beginning; and know that the changes and the gunas arise from nature.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कार्यकरणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते ।
पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते ॥
iast:
kāryakaraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtirucyate |
puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve heturucyate ||
english: Nature is said to be the cause of the body, the senses and agency; the person is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्‌क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् ।
कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥
iast:
puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijānguṇān |
kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo'sya sadasadyonijanmasu ||
english: The person, abiding in nature, experiences the gunas born of nature; attachment to the gunas is the cause of its births in good and bad wombs.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
उपद्रष्टानुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः ।
परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः ॥
iast:
upadraṣṭānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ |
paramātmeti cāpyukto dehe'sminpuruṣaḥ paraḥ ||
english: The supreme Person in this body is also called the witness, the one who consents, the sustainer, the experiencer, the great Lord and the supreme Self.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह ।
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥
iast:
ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥ saha |
sarvathā vartamāno'pi na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate ||
english: One who knows the person and nature, together with the gunas, in this way, is not born again, however they may live.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना ।
अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥
iast:
dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecidātmānamātmanā |
anye sāṃkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare ||
english: Some see the self in the self by the self through meditation; others through the yoga of knowledge; and others through the yoga of action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वान्येभ्य उपासते ।
तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥
iast:
anye tvevamajānantaḥ śrutvānyebhya upāsate |
te'pi cātitarantyeva mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ ||
english: Still others, not knowing this, worship after hearing it from others; they too, devoted to what they have heard, cross beyond death.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यावत्संजायते किंचित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
yāvatsaṃjāyate kiṃcitsattvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam |
kṣetrakṣetrajñasaṃyogāttadviddhi bharatarṣabha ||
english: Whatever is born, moving or unmoving, know that it arises from the union of the field and its knower, best of the Bharatas.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् ।
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
iast:
samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram |
vinaśyatsvavinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||
english: One who sees the supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, not perishing when they perish, truly sees.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् ।
न हिनस्त्यात्मनात्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
iast:
samaṃ paśyanhi sarvatra samavasthitamīśvaram |
na hinastyātmanātmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim ||
english: Seeing the Lord present equally everywhere, one does not harm the self by the self, and so reaches the highest goal.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः ।
यः पश्यति तथात्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति ॥
iast:
prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ |
yaḥ paśyati tathātmānamakartāraṃ sa paśyati ||
english: One who sees that all actions are done entirely by nature, and that the self is not the doer, truly sees.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति ।
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
iast:
yadā bhūtapṛthagbhāvamekasthamanupaśyati |
tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma saṃpadyate tadā ||
english: When one sees the separate existence of beings as resting in the One, and their spreading out as coming from that alone, one then attains Brahman.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः ।
शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥
iast:
anāditvānnirguṇatvātparamātmāyamavyayaḥ |
śarīrastho'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate ||
english: Because it is beginningless and beyond the gunas, this supreme Self, imperishable, does not act and is not stained, even though it dwells in the body, son of Kunti.
